clue.text: Business middling for this entertainer

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
median means in the middle, middling

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an average business is the right place for a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up who tells jokes on stage is a performer whose job is amusing audiences.

clue.text: Dawn shows a pair of birds

parts.note: the first bird is the cock, the male fowl
the second bird is the crow, a black corvid

explanation.surface: Daybreak brings a couple of birds into view.
explanation.definitionFit: Early morning, when roosters call at first light, is daybreak.

clue.text: Peculiarity of Italian art movement

definitions.meaning: a distinctive habit or idiosyncratic trait of behaviour
the sixteenth-century Italian style after the High Renaissance, with elongated figures

explanation.definitionFit: A quirky habit is an idiosyncrasy, and the same word names the late Renaissance style of Pontormo and Parmigianino.

clue.text: Debtor to confess and go under

parts.note: DR is the accountancy abbreviation for debtor
to own up is to confess or admit

explanation.surface: A debtor admits all and then goes bust.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink beneath water and perish is to go under.

clue.text: Mechanic employed in fitting part is a natural

indicators.note: employed in fitting says the letters are set inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A mechanic hired for fitting a part turns out to be a born talent.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'part is a natural', across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker, a craftsman, was once called a mechanic.

clue.text: Wrench parsnip out incomplete

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged
incomplete tells us the word parsnip loses its final letter before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook yanks a parsnip out of the ground and only part of it comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' drops the last P of PARSNIP, leaving PARSNI, which 'out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a sudden twist that injures a joint, the same as a sprained ankle or wrist.

clue.text: Grouse and nag, upset after 19 gets drunk

indicators.note: after puts the reversed word behind the rearranged letters
gets drunk means the letters of the cross-referenced answer reel about into a new order

parts.note: 19 points to the answer of 19 across, one motorway section to pass on

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word nag upside down, reading it backwards

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles and complains, upset, after a nineteenth drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets drunk' rearranges the 19 across answer into PTARMI; 'upset' reverses NAG to GAN, which 'after' puts behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird of the grouse family turns white in winter and lives in mountains and tundra.

clue.text: A move to city can bring such distress

parts.note: a go is a turn or move in a game
NY is New York, the city

explanation.surface: Relocating to the big city can cause real anguish.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense physical or mental suffering is anguish.

clue.text: Name number that is lower

parts.note: a number here is something that numbs, and ether is an old anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A clerk names a figure that is smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs: ether was an early anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower, as in the underworld or the nether regions, means beneath.

clue.text: One of three French friends following a king

indicators.note: following places the French friends after the letters for a king

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
amis is French for friends

explanation.surface: Three Frenchmen follow a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of three' is the definition: one of Dumas's Three Musketeers, alongside Athos and Porthos.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumas's swashbuckling trio of musketeers included this one, the religious-minded swordsman.

clue.text: Old song of affected piety and love

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk, affected piety
love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A singer recalls an old hymn full of pious sentiment and love.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is a section of a long poem, originally a piece to be sung, hence an old song.

clue.text: Abrupt change of policy to affect a fight

parts.note: to turn can mean to affect or alter, as milk turned by heat
a bout is a fight, as in a boxing contest

explanation.surface: A politician's sudden reversal of policy is meant to sway the outcome of a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of stance or opinion is a U-turn, a sudden switch of policy.

clue.text: In which Chinese dressmaker does the splits?

definitions.text: In which Chinese dressmaker does the splits?

parts.words: In which Chinese dressmaker does the splits?
parts.note: reads like a tailor performing gymnastics, but describes a close-fitting Chinese dress made with slits in its skirt

explanation.surface: A Chinese dressmaker is pictured doing the splits like a gymnast.
explanation.walkthrough: The splits are not acrobatics: the high-collared Chinese dress is made with splits (slits) up the side of the skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: This high-necked, close-fitting Chinese garment is traditionally cut with side slits, which the tailor makes.

clue.text: Hawthorn to survive, possibly

parts.note: may is another name for the hawthorn tree or its blossom
to be is to exist or live on, to survive

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether a hawthorn bush might pull through.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and possibly both express that something may or may not happen.

clue.text: Short circular letter

parts.note: reads like a brief mailshot, but describes the Greek letter whose name means little O, a small round character

explanation.surface: A brief circular arrives in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek name means 'little O': the short O, a circular letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet's fifteenth character is named as a small round O, a short vowel.

clue.text: Way lead, for example, is put down as aggregate

parts.note: a road is a way
lead is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: Lead and other materials are laid on a road surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken stone used for making roads is a construction aggregate.

clue.text: How sweet and kind of Daddy, giving you a start!

parts.note: a sugar daddy is a rich older man who lavishes gifts on a younger partner

indicators.note: a start means only the opening letter of the word you is taken

explanation.surface: A child thanks a generous father for a head start in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' joins the pieces; 'a start' takes the first letter of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of sugar tastes sweet, and the word also covers sentimentally sweet manners.

clue.text: Bird of prey struck window — we heard it

definitions.note: used adjectivally: belonging to or like the birds of prey

indicators.note: we heard it signals that the words before are said aloud

parts.note: struck is rapped and a window is an oriel, a bay window

explanation.surface: A hawk flew into a window, and we heard the thud.
explanation.walkthrough: An oriel is a projecting upper-storey bay window.
explanation.definitionFit: Raptors are predatory birds such as hawks and eagles, and this adjective describes them.

clue.text: Young Stephenson ran across track in study of lines and points

parts.note: GEO is the short form of George, as in George Stephenson the railway pioneer
to have run across someone is to have met them
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A young railway engineer crosses the line while studying.
explanation.walkthrough: George Stephenson built early British railways; 'Young' signals his first name shortened to GEO.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of mathematics dealing with shapes, lines, angles and points.

clue.text: One motorway section to pass on

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
M stands for motorway, as in the M1
a part is a section of something

explanation.surface: A driver explains how to overtake on a stretch of motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart news is to convey or hand it on to someone else.

clue.text: Choirboy's multiple bet?

definitions.meaning: a choirboy is a boy soprano, the highest voice part
a bet on three horses in different races, winnings carried forward

explanation.definitionFit: A boy soprano sings the highest part, and an accumulator wager on three selections has the same name.

clue.text: Sixty Roman soldiers, say, ample in deployment

indicators.note: deployment is the arrangement of troops, so the letters are redeployed into a new order

explanation.surface: Sixty Roman soldiers are judged quite enough when spread out for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployment' rearranges AMPLE IN, the word 'in' included in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of a Roman legion, numbering sixty or a hundred and twenty men, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Manners to have company in the dance

parts.note: mores are the customs and manners of a society

explanation.surface: Polite people are expected to bring a partner to the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moorish dance, related to the morris and the morisco.

clue.text: Dog these days seen in Cruft's, for example

indicators.note: seen in places the modern era inside the event

parts.note: Crufts is a famous British dog show
AD, anno domini, is the present era

explanation.surface: A dog of today appears at Crufts.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's best-known dog show. 'Dog' is a verb here: to follow someone closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow someone closely and secretly is to tail them.

clue.text: Spare-ribs establishment?

parts.note: reads like a barbecue restaurant, but spare ribs are wives, after Eve made from Adam's rib, and this is where many are kept

explanation.surface: A restaurant famous for its barbecued spare ribs.
explanation.walkthrough: Eve was made from Adam's rib, so 'spare ribs' are extra wives, and this is the household quarters where they live.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's quarters in a Muslim household, housing a man's wives and concubines.

clue.text: Received in full?

parts.note: reads like a debt paid off, but means the full radio word for the letter R, short for received

explanation.surface: A creditor confirms the debt has been paid in full.
explanation.walkthrough: In radio talk R stands for received; the word for R in the old phonetic alphabet is used to say a message was understood.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio operator's word meaning a message has come through and been understood.

clue.text: Turner, we hear, may be leaving the cast

definitions.text: Turner, we hear, may be leaving the cast

parts.words: Turner, we hear, may be leaving the cast
parts.note: reads like an actor quitting a show, but describes the creature that, as the saying goes, will turn, and that turns soil and leaves casts behind

explanation.surface: Rumour has it an actor called Turner is quitting the production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even a worm will turn', so a worm is a turner; this one turns over soil and leaves worm casts on the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing segmented invertebrate in soil, known for the coiled casts it leaves on lawns.

clue.text: Hydrogen has no smell? How uninteresting!

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
O is nothing, zero, nil
a hum is a bad smell in British slang

explanation.surface: A chemist notes that hydrogen is odourless, and finds it dull.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'hum' means a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of boredom or weary indifference at something dull.

clue.text: A kind of clock is used to speed up the ticker-rate

definitions.text: used to speed up the ticker-rate

parts.note: a digital clock shows the time in figures rather than with hands

explanation.surface: A clock is said to make the ticking go faster.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'ticker' is the heart, not the clock: this drug from foxgloves acts on the heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart drug extracted from foxglove leaves, prescribed to regulate a failing heartbeat.

clue.text: Tackle one in the army

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the word for an army

parts.note: a host is an army, a great multitude
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: One soldier is told to make a challenge within the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting gear such as a crane or winch is called tackle, block and tackle being the classic example.

clue.text: Sing a quaver

definitions.meaning: to sing with trills, as a bird does
a trilled note or a tremulous run of song

explanation.definitionFit: Birdsong is trilling, and a trill or tremolo is a quavering sound.

clue.text: Officially a class-mate

parts.note: a form is a class in a British school
an ally is a friend, a mate

explanation.surface: A pupil introduces a classmate in proper terms.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a class is called a form, such as the sixth form.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with due ceremony or authority means doing it officially.
